chunks: And when one of you sits in the sun, let him face away from it with his back, for it reveals the hidden ailment.

And when you go on pilgrimage to the House of God, the Exalted, multiply your gazing at the House of God, for God has one hundred and twenty mercies at His Sacred House: sixty for the circumambulators, forty for those who pray, and twenty for those who look.

Confess at the Multazim whatever sins you remember and whatever you do not remember, and say: 'What You have recorded upon us, record it, and what we have forgotten, forgive it for us.' For whoever confesses to his sin in that place, counts it, remembers it, and seeks forgiveness from God, it becomes incumbent upon God, the Exalted, to forgive him.
And advance your supplications before the calamity descends.

The gates of heaven are opened for you at five times: at the descent of rain, at the advance of battle, at the call to prayer, at the recitation of the Quran, at the decline of the sun, and at the rising of dawn.
Whoever among you washes a deceased person, let him perform ritual bath after he clothes him in his shrouds.
Do not put camphor on the shrouds nor anoint your dead with perfume except camphor, for the deceased is in the status of the one in Ihram.

Advise your families with good words at the time of your death, for when Fatimah bint Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) had her father pass away, all the daughters of Banu Hashim assisted her, and she said: 'Abandon the counting [of tears/groans] and stick to supplication.'
Visit your dead, for they rejoice at your visitation, and let a man seek his need at the grave of his father and mother after he supplicates for them.
The Muslim is the mirror of his brother; when you see a fault in your brother, do not be against him, but be for him as you are for yourself, guide him, advise him, and be gentle with him.
Beware of discord lest you be scattered, and adhere to moderation so you may advance and be hit [by blessings].
Whoever among you travels with a beast of burden, let him begin by feeding and watering it when he dismounts.
Do not beat the beasts on their faces, for they glorify their Lord.

And whoever among you gets lost on a journey or fears for his life, let him call: 'O Salih, help me!' For among your genie brothers is a genie named Salih who roams the lands for your sake, accounting himself for you; when he hears the voice, he answers, guides the lost among you, and holds his beast for you.
Whoever fears a lion for himself or his flock, let him draw a line around them and say: 'O God, Lord of Daniel and the Den, and Lord of every lion that is tamed, protect me and protect my flock.'
And whoever fears a scorpion, let him recite these verses: 'Peace upon Noah among the nations. Thus indeed do We reward the doers of good. Indeed, he was of Our believing servants.'

Whoever fears drowning, let him recite: 'In the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage; indeed my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful. In the name of Allah, the King, the Truth. And they did not appraise Allah with true appraisal, and the whole earth will be [grasped] by His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be rolled in His right hand; exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.'

Shave the hair of your children on the seventh day and give charity when you shave them, silver equal in weight to their hair, to a Muslim. Thus did the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) do with al-Hasan, al-Husayn, and the rest of his offspring.
When you give something to the beggar, ask him to supplicate for you, for he will be answered for you and not for himself, because they lie.

And let the one who gives bring his hand to his mouth and kiss it, for God, the Exalted, takes it before it falls into the hand of the beggar, as God, the Exalted, said: 'Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and receives charities?'
Give charity at night, for charity at night extinguishes the anger of the Lord, may His Majesty be Exalted.
Consider your speech as part of your deeds; minimize your speech except in good.

Spend from what God has provided you, for the spender is in the status of the one who strives in the way of God. Whoever is certain of the return will be generous and his soul will be willing to spend.
Whoever is certain and then doubts, let him proceed upon his certainty, for doubt does not invalidate certainty.

key_terms.الْمُلْتَزِم: The Multazim (place between the Kaaba and the wall)

ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical and ritual teachings of Imam Ali regarding daily life, Hajj, and social conduct?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* encapsulates the Shia tradition of *Hikmah* (wisdom), blending practical daily etiquette with deep spiritual psychology, such as the concept of 'confessing sins' at the Multazim to ensure divine forgiveness. It highlights the interconnectedness of ritual purity, social brotherhood (*Ukhuwwah*), and reliance on divine protection through specific supplications, reflecting the comprehensive nature of Imam Ali’s teachings for holistic Muslim life.
